name: law_firm_software_012_firmwide_conflict_of_interest_audit
instruction: Run the firmwide conflict-of-interest audit, batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta). The firm is litigating matters where the party on the other side is itself a client of the firm on other matters, and leadership wants every such tangle found. Apply the firm's intake conflict-screen rule (INTAKE-01 in firm_policies) across the whole existing contact book: a contact is conflicted when its organisation matches a client under the policy's name-matching rule AND the contact is linked (via its matter_ids) to a matter whose own client is a different client -- the firm's own client-side contacts sitting on their own client's matters are not conflicts. For every conflict found, push one ops_reports row (report='conflict_of_interest', batch_code) naming the contact, the matched client, and the conflicted matter, with a note diagnosing why the pair is a conflict. Then give each conflict its severity: one ops_reports row per conflict (report='conflict_severity', batch_code) -- high when the conflicted matter's current status is open, low otherwise. Finally push one summary row (report='conflict_of_interest_summary', batch_code) with the number of conflicts found; a clean sweep pushes only that summary row. No other ops_reports rows for this batch under those three report names may exist. Mutate nothing. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: One real conflict exists in production data (planted: 1, snapshot-confirmed): contact Mary Johnson's organisation matches client Tech Innovations Inc while she is linked to matter 2026-001, whose client is Acme Corporation -- the firm is litigating against its own client's company. Bulk contacts use a disjoint ' Group'-suffixed organisation pool, so the finding stays a precise needle, not scale noise.

3 same-organisation same-client near-miss contacts (General Counsel Tech -> matters 2026-003/007, Green Earth Liaison -> 2026-004, State AG Liaison -> 2026-005; snapshot-confirmed: 3 contacts / 4 contact-matter pairs) match client names exactly but their linked matters belong to the matched client itself -- an audit matching on name alone over-reports by exactly 3 and FAILs; the matched client must DIFFER from the linked matter's client.

Former-client matters 2026-008 (closed ~400 days ago, inside any 2-6 year window) and 2026-009 (closed ~2600 days ago, outside) are matters, not contacts: an audit that sweeps matter names or applies INTAKE-01's former-client window as the audit's flag condition mis-flags them (snapshot-confirmed pair present); the organisation-match rule is the only flag basis here.

success_criteria.summary: Exactly one conflict_of_interest row (Mary Johnson / Tech Innovations Inc / matter 2026-001) found via the INTAKE-01 normalized organisation match with the different-client condition, one conflict_severity row per conflict from the conflicted matter's live status, and one conflict_of_interest_summary row with conflicts_found matching the conflict set. The 3 same-org same-client near-miss contacts are never flagged (name-only matching over-reports by 3 and FAILs). contacts/clients/matters untouched; dual-path confirmed.

checks.expect: exactly the INTAKE-01 conflict set (1 row), one severity row per conflict, one summary row; near-miss contacts absent
name-only matching over-reports by 3 (the same-org same-client near-misses) and FAILs; the severity lookup targets the conflicted matter's live status
conflict set and summary agree between Python-derived expectations and SQL over the written rows

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: v2 moves the conflict definition into INTAKE-01: the agent must apply the policy's NORMALIZED name matching (which decides that the near-miss dba variants ARE the same organisation) plus the different-client condition -- a name-only audit over-reports by exactly 3 on this snapshot (3 same-org same-client near-miss contacts planted) and FAILs. Distinct from task 006's create-time gate: this is a retrospective firmwide sweep over the existing contact/client/matter graph (803 contacts x 500 clients x 2002 matters).
